description.fun: A bundle of energy that can't sit still: Scorbunny warms up with a run until fire energy courses through its body and the pads on its feet and nose blaze with heat. Hot enough to start small fires, those footpads hit hard when it kicks. The yellow mark across its nose comes from a Japanese character trope, a plaster on the nose that marks a rambunctious kid.
description.guide: The Fire-type first partner Pokémon of Galar, from Pokémon Sword and Shield. Scorbunny runs to warm up, sending fire energy to pads on its feet and nose that grow hot enough to burn. It evolves into Raboot and then Cinderace.
description.tagline: A sprinting bunny whose feet heat up for fiery kicks

description.fun: Raboot looks dressed for training, its fluffy fur worn like a tracksuit and snood. The fur keeps out the cold and lets it use hotter fire moves. It practises footwork by kicking Berries off branches and juggling them, hands tucked into its fur so its feet do all the work.
description.guide: The middle stage of Scorbunny's line. Raboot's thick, fluffy fur keeps it warm and powers hotter fire moves, and it trains its kicks by juggling Berries. It is the lightest of the middle-stage first partner Pokémon.
description.tagline: Juggles Berries with its feet to sharpen its footwork

description.fun: Galar's star striker juggles a pebble with its feet until it becomes a blazing Pyro Ball, then puts spin on it so opponents can't dodge. It gets pumped up when cheered on, though showing off can land it in trouble. Its Hidden Ability, Libero, is named after a position in football, the sport its whole design draws on.
description.guide: The final evolution of Scorbunny and Galar's Fire-type first partner. Cinderace turns pebbles into flaming balls that it kicks at opponents, a design drawn from football players. It has a Gigantamax form.
description.tagline: A footballer rabbit that kicks pebbles into fireballs

description.fun: Rides a fireball that can grow over 90 metres across and, fuelled by Cinderace's fighting spirit, chases foes down as if it has a mind of its own. It arrived with The Isle of Armor.
